source_snapshot.procedure: From BMC console, HTTP GET `/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory/`; check GPU FW.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES with hardcoded plain HTTP and raw user inspection.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: FULLY AUTOMATABLE after stable GPU-member mapping and approved version matrix.

old_problem: The collection URI is standard, but the source uses a hardcoded insecure endpoint and supplies no installed-GPU topology, member mapping or expected version matrix; collection readability alone does not prove GPU firmware correctness.
disposition_reason: DMTF Redfish defines FirmwareInventory as a SoftwareInventoryCollection and standard member resources. ED-03 permits topology and approved version values as project configuration. The review can therefore close with complete member enumeration, stable identity mapping and a supplied version/compatibility matrix; no firmware update is involved.
decision_basis: Direct XLSX rows 2257 and 2258, same-row AI fields, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed.
DMTF DSP2046 lists `/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory` as the standard SoftwareInventoryCollection URI; member resources carry software inventory identity/version data.
Bind SUT/BMC and installed GPU topology, enumerate the complete collection and dereference every candidate member rather than assuming the first entry.
Map by approved stable identifiers/RelatedItem/OEM identity and compare normalized versions against the signed per-GPU or approved aggregate matrix.
Use verified HTTPS and protected authentication; capture raw collection/member JSON and report missing, duplicate or ambiguous mappings distinctly.
No authentication, Redfish GET, firmware update, flash or DUT action occurred.

test_case.purpose: Prove every intended installed GPU or approved GPU aggregate maps to a complete Redfish firmware inventory member whose active version matches the project matrix.
required_package: Bound SUT/BMC and installed GPU topology
Per-device or aggregate firmware version/compatibility matrix and normalization
Trusted TLS, protected credentials and Redfish JSON client
test_case.test_command: Issue TLS-validated GETs to the FirmwareInventory collection and every member; preserve raw HTTP/JSON, map installed GPUs using the approved stable identifiers/relations, normalize versions only by the supplied rule and compare each required device/aggregate to the matrix.
test_case.expected_result: All installed GPUs are covered exactly once or by an explicitly approved aggregate, every required member is healthy/complete, and each normalized active firmware version equals an approved compatible value with no missing, duplicate or ambiguous mapping.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires complete collection/member evidence, deterministic topology mapping and matrix match. Missing/duplicate/ambiguous members or version mismatch is FAIL. Missing runtime topology/matrix blocks execution, not review; readable JSON alone cannot pass.
safety_gate: Verified HTTPS BMC identity and protected credentials.
GET collection/members only; never invoke update actions.
Do not infer device mapping from member order or display name alone.
Stop on incomplete pagination, malformed JSON or ambiguous identity.
expected_evidence: Each relevant member JSON and stable identity relations
GPU-to-member coverage table and aggregation approval
test_case.recovery: No mutation is expected; on mapping or transport ambiguity stop, preserve raw evidence and obtain corrected runtime mapping without flashing or changing inventory.

source_conflict.reason: The source consistently requests read-only GPU firmware inventory; version/topology inputs are parameters.

blocked.reason: Standard Redfish resources define the method and project bindings can be supplied at runtime.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: SUT/BMC/GPU topology, stable member/aggregate mapping, approved firmware matrix/normalization and TLS credentials.
pending.execution_status: REVIEW RESOLVED AS PARAMETERIZED READ-ONLY REDFISH INVENTORY; NO DUT ACTION EXECUTED
pending.owner: GPU firmware/platform owner supplies topology and matrix; end engineer owns verdict
pending.unlock_condition: Bind mapping and approved versions before execution; these do not reopen review.
